items.headline: Social Security checks rise 3.6% in January, about $75 a month
items.caption: The 2027 cost-of-living raise covers 76 million people on Social Security and SSI. It is the biggest bump since 2023. SSI recipients see it first, on Dec 31.

visual.title: 2027 COLA
visual.label: Raise for Social Security and SSI, starting with January payments.

detail: The Social Security Administration set the 2027 cost-of-living adjustment at 3.6%, based on the CPI-W inflation index. Nearly 72 million Social Security beneficiaries get it starting in January, and about 7.3 million SSI recipients get it on December 31.
It follows raises of 2.8% for 2026 and 2.5% for 2025, and is the largest since the 8.7% jump in 2023.
If you want to see your notice online, set up a my Social Security account and choose paperless notices by November 18. Paper notices go out by mail in December.
money: Update your 2027 budget with the new amount once your notice arrives.
Still working? The cap on wages hit by Social Security tax rises to $192,300, so high earners pay a bit more.
If you are retired and have savings, the raise is a reminder to keep cash in accounts that beat inflation.
risk: Medicare premium changes for 2027 are set separately and can eat part of the raise.

items.headline: IRS raises 2027 tax brackets and the standard deduction
items.caption: The IRS adjusted nearly 70 tax rules for inflation. Single filers get a $16,600 standard deduction, married couples $33,200. Rates stay the same.
detail: The adjustments apply to the 2027 tax year, so they show up on returns filed in 2028 and in paycheck withholding during 2027. Tax rates themselves did not change.
Brackets are indexed to chained CPI. Inflation reached 3.7% in September, so the increases were sizable and in line with forecasts.
About 86% of filers take the standard deduction instead of itemizing.
money: Higher brackets mean slightly less tax withheld from 2027 paychecks; check your first January pay stub.
If your itemized deductions are close to the standard amount, "bunching" donations into one year can push you over.
Families: the Child Tax Credit rises to $2,300 per child for 2027.
risk: Your actual savings depend on income, filing status and credits.

items.headline: Your 401(k) limit is expected to rise to $25,500 in 2027
items.caption: The IRS has not announced it yet, but Milliman’s final forecast points to a $1,000 increase. HSA limits are already official: $4,500 self-only, $9,000 family.
detail: Milliman’s final forecast, based on September inflation data, estimates a roughly 3.5% increase factor for 2027 retirement limits. Last year the IRS announced the 2026 limits on November 13.
Health Savings Account limits use a different formula and were published in May: $4,500 for self-only coverage and $9,000 for family coverage.
money: Set your 401(k) contribution percentage in December so January paychecks start at the higher limit.
An HSA is the only account that is tax-free going in, growing and coming out for medical costs.
Self-employed? A Solo 401(k) lets you contribute as both employee and employer.
risk: 401(k) and IRA figures are projections until the IRS publishes its notice.

items.headline: Standard deduction or itemize? The 30-second test
items.caption: Which one lowers your taxes, using the new 2027 numbers.

scenes.s: You get to subtract whichever is bigger from your taxable income.
A flat amount, no receipts. For 2027: $16,600 single, $33,200 married.
Add up mortgage interest, state and local taxes, and charitable donations.

scenes.say: If your itemized total beats sixteen thousand six hundred dollars, itemize. If not, take the standard.

scenes.s: For most people it wins without any paperwork.
Close to the line? Group two years of donations into one year and itemize that year.

items.headline: ACA open enrollment is live, and benchmark premiums are up 13%
items.caption: It is the second double-digit jump in a row: benchmark plans cost 42% more than in 2025. Most enrollees still get subsidies, but not above 400% of the poverty level.

visual.title: 2027 ACA marketplace
visual.label: Average rise in benchmark silver premiums for 2027.

detail: Open enrollment for 2027 coverage started November 1 in most states. The enhanced premium tax credits expired at the end of 2025, and paid enrollment fell 12% to 19.2 million by February 2026.

Deadlines shifted this year. Healthinsurance.org says enrollment ends December 15 in HealthCare.gov states and cannot run past December 31 anywhere; some news reports still cite January 15. Check your state’s exchange.
New Mexico fully replaced the lost federal help for its residents in 2026, and its enrollment grew while the national total fell.
money: Do not auto-renew. Insurers are leaving some markets and the cheapest plan last year may not be this year.
Estimate your income carefully: subsidies are based on it, and underestimating means paying some back at tax time.
A bronze plan paired with an HSA can be cheaper for healthy people who want tax-free savings.
risk: Missing the deadline usually means no coverage until next year unless you have a qualifying life event.

items.headline: SNAP changes this fall: new work rules, new limits, new store rules
items.caption: Benefit amounts rose with inflation on Oct 1, but work requirements now reach most adults up to 64, some noncitizens lose eligibility, and stores face new stocking rules.

visual.title: SNAP: what changed
items: Oct 1: benefit amounts and income limits adjusted up for inflation
Work rules: most adults through age 64 need 80 hours a month
Some noncitizens without green cards lose eligibility
Nov 4: new stocking standards for stores that take SNAP
Several states now restrict candy and soda purchases

detail: The new federal fiscal year brought higher maximum benefits, higher income limits and a bigger minimum benefit on October 1.

Last year’s budget law also widened work requirements: able-bodied adults now must log 80 hours a month of work or training to keep benefits beyond three months, and the age range extends through 64. Eligibility for some noncitizens was removed.
Updated stocking standards for most SNAP-authorized stores began November 4, and some states have restricted candy and soda.
money: If you or a family member gets SNAP, report work hours on time; missing paperwork is a common reason benefits stop.
In California, CalFresh shoppers can also get up to $60 a month back on produce at participating stores.
Food banks and school meal programs can fill gaps if benefits are cut.
risk: Rules vary by state; check your state SNAP agency for how the changes apply to your case.

items.headline: Raises coming Jan 1: 17 states lift the minimum wage
items.caption: Washington hits $17.73, Connecticut $17.48 and California $17.40. Michigan gets the biggest jump, $1.27. Twenty states stay at the federal $7.25.
detail: Seventeen states change their minimum wage on January 1, 2027, many through automatic inflation adjustments. New Jersey goes to $16.48 for most workers, Colorado to $15.71 and Virginia to $13.75.
Florida reached $15 on September 30, 2026. Alaska goes to $15 on July 1, 2027, and Hawaii jumps to $18 in January 2028.
Many cities set higher local rates; dozens in California and Washington also rise on January 1.
money: A $1.27 raise is worth about $2,642 a year for a full-time worker, before taxes.
Business owners: budget the new payroll now and update required workplace posters.
Expect January price bumps at restaurants and services in states with big increases.
risk: Some state rates were still pending final announcement; confirm your state’s labor department page.

Senior property tax relief · Nov installment

detail: New York’s Protecting Our Wallets Energy Rebate, a one-time payment in the 2026–27 budget, pays $100 to $200. Payments are automatic and arrival dates vary even between neighbors.
Pennsylvania’s Property Tax/Rent Rebate Program pays $380 to $1,000 to qualifying older adults and people with disabilities, and applications can be filed until the end of 2026.

New Jersey’s Stay NJ program pays seniors up to $6,500 in property tax relief in quarterly installments. Michigan says its expanded working families credit averaged $836 for about 653,000 recipients last year.
money: Most of these are automatic, but some require an application with a deadline; Pennsylvania’s closes at year end.
Tell older relatives in these states; property tax relief programs are often missed.
State rebates are generally not taxed federally, but confirm with IRS guidance or a tax pro.
risk: Amounts and eligibility depend on income and filing history.

items.headline: ICE faces new scrutiny from judges, Congress and voters
items.caption: An Oregon judge found an ICE officer lied in an arrest report. House Democrats are demanding answers on US citizens held by agents. NPR reported voters rebuked the raids at the polls.

visual.title: Immigration enforcement this week
items: Oregon: judge finds ICE officer lied in an arrest report
House Democrats press for answers on detained US citizens
ICE plans to deport some Afghans through Pakistan, an official says
An indicted officer had served just over a year amid a hiring surge
New Democratic Congress in January means oversight hearings

detail: The administration has expanded ICE operations with tens of billions of dollars in added funding and has widened enforcement to all undocumented immigrants, according to the Council on Foreign Relations.

This week a federal judge in Oregon found an ICE officer lied in an arrest report and that the agency violated his order. After a ProPublica investigation, House Democrats demanded answers about US citizens detained by immigration agents.

NPR reported that voters rebuked the administration’s raids at the polls. With Democrats taking both chambers in January, expect more oversight hearings, while enforcement itself is run by the executive branch.
money: Industries that rely on immigrant labor, like construction, farming and hospitality, face staffing pressure, which can push up wages and prices.
Employers: keep I-9 paperwork current; worksite audits carry fines.
Families with mixed status may want to talk to an immigration attorney about plans for property and accounts.
risk: This is a fast-moving story with court rulings changing week to week.

detail: WARN Act notices, which large employers must file ahead of mass layoffs, covered about 1,528 workers in the first week of November, all in New Jersey. Verizon accounted for most of them at its Basking Ridge headquarters.
The total was far below the same week in 2025, when 17,418 workers received notices.
Earlier in 2026, companies including Amazon, UPS and Oracle announced large cuts.
money: If you are laid off, file for unemployment right away; benefits usually start from the filing date.
Losing job-based health insurance lets you enroll in an ACA plan outside open enrollment, often cheaper than COBRA.
Severance is often negotiable, especially for unused vacation and health coverage.

items.caption: Gas prices pushed annual inflation to 3.7% in September. That set the 3.6% Social Security raise and the IRS bracket changes, and it is why the Fed may hike in December.
detail: Inflation climbed to 3.7% in September as gas prices kept household costs rising, according to Money.
Those numbers flow straight into your finances: they set the 2027 Social Security COLA, the IRS inflation adjustments and the Fed’s next move.
With a strong October jobs report, futures traders see about a 77% chance the Fed raises rates on December 9.
money: Cash earning less than 3.7% is losing value. Compare high-yield savings, CDs and Treasury bills.
Use the inflation number when asking for a raise: a 3% raise is a pay cut in real terms.
Lock in fixed rates on loans before a possible hike if you were already planning to borrow.

items.headline: Employers are switching how they pay for health insurance
items.caption: Adoption of ICHRAs, where a company gives workers a set amount to buy their own plan, jumped 53% in 2026 as group insurance costs climbed.
detail: An individual coverage HRA lets an employer reimburse workers tax-free for individual health plans instead of running a group plan. Large and small employers adopted them 53% more in 2026.
Employers like the fixed cost; workers can keep the plan if they change jobs.
It overlaps with self-employed and small-business buyers, who are also feeling rising marketplace premiums.
money: Small business owners: an ICHRA can cap health benefit costs while still offering coverage.
Employees offered an ICHRA can shop marketplace plans with the allowance, tax-free.
Compare: if the allowance makes coverage "affordable," you may lose ACA subsidy eligibility.
risk: Plan choice and costs depend heavily on your local marketplace.

items.headline: OpenAI cuts Cursor off on Nov 12 after SpaceX buys the coding app
items.caption: OpenAI will stop supplying its models to Cursor on November 12. From November 20, new OpenAI rules require approval for model routers and AI gateways.

items.t: Cursor loses access to OpenAI models
items.s: After SpaceX acquired the coding tool
Routers and AI gateways need approval; direct-access services treated separately

detail: OpenAI said it will stop supplying models to Cursor, the AI coding editor, on November 12, 2026, after SpaceX bought the tool.

Separately, OpenAI’s updated usage policies take effect November 20. They distinguish services that resell direct model access from apps that use OpenAI models inside their own features, and require approval for model routers and gateways.
The moves show AI labs tightening control over who can resell their models.
money: If your business or side project runs on one AI vendor, build in a backup; access can change with weeks of notice.
Coding tools that support several model providers protect you from these cutoffs.
Platform fights create openings for tools and freelancers who help companies switch.
risk: Details of enforcement are still emerging.

California put $20 million into restarting its CalFresh produce rebate after federal SNAP changes cut average benefits.
Where you live increasingly decides how much help you get with health care, food and energy bills.

Small business owners in generous states may find employees value state benefits in their pay decisions.

items.headline: Nasdaq 100 has its worst day since 2020 as chip stocks get crushed
items.caption: Two days after Democrats won Congress, investors dumped AI and chip stocks on fears of tighter rules for data centers. About $3 trillion in value vanished in one session.

visual.title: Thursday, Nov 5 close
visual.label: Nasdaq 100. The S&P 500 fell 4.35% and the Dow lost 1,833 points.

detail: The selloff hit memory and storage makers hardest, then spread to chip equipment and data-center suppliers. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell about 12%, its biggest one-day drop since 2020, and every one of the 30 Dow stocks closed lower.

The trigger was political. Democrats won control of both chambers, including in states where data-center growth has been contentious, and investors priced in slower AI buildouts and more regulation. Senators Sanders and Ocasio-Cortez are pushing a bill for a data-center moratorium.
Perspective matters: SanDisk was still up more than 200% for 2026 after the drop, and Micron about 130%. The Nasdaq Composite is now officially in a correction, down 10% from its October 6 record.
money: Corrections are when long-term buyers get better prices. If you already invest, keep your scheduled buys running instead of stopping.
Broad index funds spread the risk. A single chip stock can drop 20% in a day; an S&P 500 fund fell 4.35%.
Write down a watchlist and target prices now, while you are calm, instead of deciding mid-panic.
risk: Regulation fears may not be priced in yet; dips can keep dipping.
Never use margin or borrowed money to "buy the dip."

items.headline: Crash week? How regular people turn drops into discounts
items.caption: Dollar-cost averaging, explained with real math in under a minute.

scenes.t: Stocks just had their worst day since 2020.
scenes.s: Here is how regular investors turn crashes into discounts.
Invest the same dollar amount on a schedule. Every week, no matter what the market does.
Same $100, different prices:
scenes.say: Same hundred dollars each week. At fifty dollars you get two shares. At twenty-five, you get four.

scenes.s: Your average cost is $38.10, while the average price was $41.25. The dip did the work.
scenes.say: Ten and a half shares for four hundred dollars. Your average cost is thirty-eight ten, below the average price of forty-one twenty-five.

scenes.s: Use broad index funds, not one hype stock. And never borrowed money.

items.headline: Democrats take both the House and Senate in a midterm landslide
items.caption: Seven Senate seats flipped, including Texas, where James Talarico beat Ken Paxton. Republicans lose their trifecta; divided government starts in January.
detail: Democrats needed to flip four Senate seats and gained seven, including a seat in South Carolina, where the party had not won a Senate race since 1998. In the House, Democrats were on pace for their largest majority since 2008.
Hakeem Jeffries is on track to become the first Black House speaker; he needs 218 votes when the new Congress convenes on January 3. Democratic leadership elections are the week of November 16.

President Trump congratulated Democrats while distancing himself from the losses. With a Republican president and a Democratic Congress, expect more investigations and fewer big new laws through 2028.
money: Gridlock usually means fewer surprise tax or spending changes, which markets tend to like over time.
Sectors Congress targets with hearings move first. This week that was AI data centers and chipmakers.
Big new federal programs are unlikely before 2028, so plan around current tax rules, not campaign promises.
risk: Two Senate races and many House seats were still being counted when this was written.

Pay down variable-rate debt like credit cards first; those rates climb with every Fed hike.

visual.label: Lower oil is good for drivers and airlines, bad for energy stocks.

detail: Prices fell more than 7% on November 2 alone as Iranian and Qatari officials held days of talks on ending the war between Iran and the United States and Israel. President Trump said a deal "could happen."
Brent had finished October at a six-month high on fears fighting would escalate after the midterms. Talks over a Russia–Ukraine settlement added to the downward pressure.
No agreement has been signed. The drop reflects expectations, not a return to normal shipping, and Goldman Sachs has warned prices can snap back if talks fail.
money: Gas prices tend to follow crude with a lag, so fill-up costs could ease over the next few weeks.
Airlines, trucking and delivery companies benefit from cheaper fuel; energy producers lose.
If you are hedging against war risk, this is a reminder that peace headlines can erase gains in days.
risk: A collapse in talks or a new attack on tankers could send oil back up fast.

sources.t: The Iran war isn’t over, but oil traders are pricing in peace

items.headline: Tariff check: the China truce now runs to Jan 10, and a new levy hits Nov 10
items.caption: The US–China truce was pushed back two months. A 25% tariff on Chinese cargo-handling equipment is scheduled for Tuesday, and Canada’s 50% tariff on $20B of goods is in force.

items.s: Government ordered to refund about $166 billion
Extended from Nov 10 during Xi’s September visit

detail: The November 2025 deal with China cut reciprocal tariffs to a flat 10% through November 10, 2026. During Xi Jinping’s September visit to Washington, both sides agreed to extend that truce to January 10, 2027.

Separately, a 25% tariff on Chinese-origin maritime and cargo-handling equipment is scheduled to start November 10. Average US tariffs have risen from about 2% to 10% in two years, and the goods trade deficit hit a record.
Tariff revenue fell for the first time since February, according to recent data, partly because of the court-ordered refunds.
money: Resellers and small importers: if you sell China-made goods, buying inventory before Jan 10 locks in today’s 10% rate in case talks fail.
If your business paid the voided emergency tariffs, check with your customs broker about refund claims.
Expect price swings on imported electronics, tools and home goods around each deadline; that is where flip margins open and close.
risk: Deadlines have been moved many times; plans built on one date can break.

scenes.t: A tariff is a tax on imports.

scenes.s: After the Supreme Court struck down the emergency tariffs in February, importers got paid back.

items.headline: Deal week: Marvell agrees to buy Lumentum in a $115B all-stock deal
items.caption: Plus Shield buying Echodyne for $5.3B and a $1.6B bid for Helen of Troy. China blocked SoftBank’s $5.4B purchase of ABB’s robotics unit.
detail: Marvell’s purchase of optical-component maker Lumentum is an all-stock deal valued around $115 billion, a bet on the AI networking gear inside data centers. Defense-tech firm Shield agreed to buy radar maker Echodyne for $5.3 billion.
Oaktree-backed Empower Brands proposed buying consumer-products company Helen of Troy for $1.6 billion, and SpaceX is reportedly exploring a purchase of EchoStar’s Boost Mobile.

Regulators remain the wild card: China blocked SoftBank’s $5.4 billion ABB robotics deal, according to the FT. In the US, comments on the $85 billion Union Pacific–Norfolk Southern merger are due November 18.
money: Merger arbitrage: a target’s stock usually trades a bit below the deal price. That gap is what traders earn if the deal closes.
In all-stock deals like Marvell–Lumentum, the payout moves with the buyer’s share price, so the target falls when the buyer falls.
Blocked deals show the downside: the target can drop back to where it was before the announcement.
risk: Spreads are small for a reason. A failed deal can wipe out years of small gains.

items.headline: Bitcoin slides under $78K as risk appetite fades
items.caption: Bitcoin fell 4.8% in the last week of October, ether 6% and solana 6.4%. After the midterms, traders are watching $82,000 as the level that flips the trend.

visual.title: Crypto, week ending Oct 30
visual.foot: Bitcoin sits roughly 40% below its record.

detail: Crypto followed tech stocks lower as investors pulled back from speculative assets. Bitcoin closed the week at about $77,198, ether near $2,241 and solana around $96.
A December rate hike would be a headwind: higher rates make holding assets with no yield less attractive.
After the election, crypto analysts flagged $82,000 as the key resistance level. Bitcoin’s record is $126,198, set in October 2025.
money: If you buy crypto, small recurring buys reduce the risk of going all-in at a bad price.
Keep crypto a small slice of what you invest; a 40% drawdown from the high is normal for bitcoin.
Track your cost basis now. Crypto sales are taxable, and losses can offset gains.
risk: Crypto is highly volatile and has little consumer protection.
Avoid leverage; liquidations hit hardest on fast drops.

items.headline: Friday bounce: tech claws back, and AI power stocks surge
items.caption: The Nasdaq rose 1.1% and fear eased, but the S&P 500 still logged its worst week since April 2025. Vistra jumped about 11% and NRG about 10%.
detail: Stocks steadied after Thursday’s rout. AI stocks recovered some losses, while the Dow slipped as a hot jobs report pushed Treasury yields and the dollar higher.
The standouts were companies that power data centers: Vistra rose about 11% after earnings, NRG Energy about 10% and Quanta Services 6%.
The VIX, Wall Street’s fear gauge, fell 9% but stayed elevated above 25.
money: Companies that already own valuable infrastructure, like power plants and grid builders, held up better than those that depend on building more.
A VIX above 20 means bigger daily swings; size positions smaller until it calms down.
Options get expensive when the VIX is high, which favors selling covered calls on stocks you already own over buying options.
risk: One green day does not end a correction.

items.headline: California: Becerra wins governor, the billionaire tax is failing
items.caption: Xavier Becerra becomes the state’s first Latino governor. Prop 40’s wealth tax trails, while Prop 42, which bans new state taxes on investments, is passing.

rows.s: No new taxes on stocks & accounts

detail: Becerra, the former US health secretary, replaces Gavin Newsom, who is termed out. Results come from early counts; California accepts mail ballots postmarked by Election Day, and certification comes in early December.

Prop 40 would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on net worth above $1 billion to fund health care. Opponents spent more than $300 million against it and backed Props 41 and 42, which were written to cancel it if they got more yes votes. Prop 41 was failing; Prop 42 was passing.

Prop 3, which makes the existing higher income-tax rates on earnings over about $371,000 permanent instead of expiring in 2031, led in early returns. Prop 45, which would speed up environmental reviews, was trailing.
money: Prop 42 passing means no new state tax on financial assets like brokerage and investment accounts.
Prop 1 housing bonds mean more state money for affordable housing; watch for new local application windows.
High earners: if Prop 3 holds, plan around today’s top California rates staying in place past 2031.
risk: Counts can shift for days; close measures may flip before certification.

items.headline: CalFresh users can get up to $60 a month in free produce again
items.caption: The Fruit and Vegetable EBT program is back with $20 million after running dry in June. The rebate applies automatically at participating stores, for a limited time.

visual.title: California program
visual.label: Instant rebate on fruits and vegetables for CalFresh households.
facts: Through the end of the year

detail: The CalFresh Fruit and Vegetable EBT Program gives an instant rebate when CalFresh shoppers buy fresh produce at participating stores. It was suspended in June after its money ran out.
Assemblymember Alex Lee secured $20 million in the 2026–27 budget to restart it. Since 2023 it has served more than 546,000 Californians.
The state says the program is not expanding to new stores, so check that your store is still taking part before you shop.
money: If you get CalFresh, shopping at a participating store can stretch your benefits by up to $60 a month.
Know someone on CalFresh? Share it: many people missed it because there is no sign-up.
Federal changes are cutting average CalFresh benefits by about $39 a month for many households, so this offsets a real loss.
risk: Funding is limited and could run out before year end.

items.headline: AI race: Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon takes #1, Tencent drops a giant open model
items.caption: Gemini 4 Carbon topped the LMArena leaderboard. Tencent released Hy4, a 770-billion-parameter open-weights model. OpenAI says ChatGPT search is now a fifth of Google’s volume.
detail: Gemini 4 Carbon took the top spot on the LMArena text leaderboard with a rating of 1528. OpenAI released LifeVal, a benchmark that measures how well models handle practical tasks such as government paperwork and vehicle inspections.
Tencent’s Hy4 is an open-weights mixture-of-experts model with 770 billion parameters and a one-million-token context window, part of a wave of cheaper models squeezing AI prices.
On the policy side, China said it is speeding up laws to oversee algorithms and computing power, while in the US the new Democratic majority has spooked investors about data-center rules.
money: Open-weights models keep pushing AI costs down; if you pay for AI tools in a side business, shop around every few months.
Skills that combine AI with a niche (reselling listings, video editing, paperwork) are where freelancers are getting paid.
Using AI more is not the same as AI stocks going up: this week usage grew while chip stocks fell.
risk: Leaderboards change weekly; avoid locking into one paid tool long-term.

items.headline: Bankruptcy watch: franchise operators keep cracking
items.caption: A 30-restaurant Denny’s operator, a Mattress Firm franchisee and candy brand Stuckey’s all filed for Chapter 11. High rents and softer spending are squeezing small chains.
detail: EYM Diner, which runs about 30 Denny’s restaurants in Texas, is the latest bankruptcy tied to former mega-franchisee EYM Group. D&A Mattress, a Mattress Firm franchisee in Texas and New Mexico, filed on November 2.

Franchise operators have filed in clusters throughout 2026, citing high lease costs, weaker spending on non-essentials and tighter credit. Bain expects global luxury sales to shrink for a second straight year.
Chapter 11 lets a company keep operating while it restructures; Stuckey’s says its brand will continue.
money: Liquidation and closing sales can be a source of cheap inventory for resellers; watch local auction and liquidation listings.
Use gift cards from struggling chains soon; they can lose value in bankruptcy.
Rising franchise failures are an early signal of consumer stress, a reason to favor steadier companies.
risk: Restructured companies can still liquidate later.

items.caption: vVardis, which sells an over-the-counter cavity treatment, and Rezera, an inflammation-drug developer, aim to raise about $200M each. New issues are down 4% this year.

rows.s: Insiders free to sell this week

detail: vVardis plans to raise about $214 million at a market value near $1.3 billion; most of its revenue comes from its over-the-counter US product. Rezera’s lead drug, ruvonoflast, heads into Phase 3 trials in the first half of 2027.
Newly public stocks have lagged: the Renaissance IPO Index was down 4.0% for the year as of November 5, while the S&P 500 was up 8.4%.
Nine lock-up periods expire this week, which can add selling pressure to recent IPOs.
money: Small biotech IPOs are binary bets on trial results; size any position as money you can afford to lose.
Check lock-up calendars before buying a recent IPO; prices often sag around expiration.
An IPO ETF spreads risk across many new listings instead of betting on one.
risk: Price ranges can change or deals can be postponed in a volatile market.
